test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 12 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Vimal secured 46% marks in the exam and failed to qualify in the exam by 10 marks. If he secured 52% marks, he would have secured 8 marks more than what was the minimum qualifying marks. What were the minimum marks one had to score to qualify in the exam?
solution:
Given: 

Vimal secured 46% marks in the exam and failed to qualify in the exam by 10 marks.

If he secured 52% marks, he would have secured 8 marks more than what was the minimum qualifying marks.

Calculation:

Let the total marks in the exam be Q.

Vimal scored = 46% × Q = 0.46Q

Minimum passing marks = 0.46Q + 10

According to the question,

0.46Q + 10 = 52% × Q - 8

⇒ 0.46Q + 10 = 0.52Q - 8

⇒ 0.52Q - 0.46Q = 10 + 8

⇒ 0.06Q = 18

⇒ Q = 18/0.06

⇒ Q = 300

Now, the passing marks in the exam

⇒ 0.46 × 300 + 10

⇒ 148

**∴ The minimum marks one had to score to qualify in the exam were 148.**
